notes: The page's six example sentences ('What is the weather like in your city?') are excluded.
'clime' dropped and 'climate' added in its place at Leon's call. 'Clime' is archaic and
poetic; a learner taught it would say 'the clime in Medellin', which sounds bizarre rather
than merely wrong. It sits beside 'weather' so the unit can teach the difference — Spanish
uses tiempo and clima the same way English uses weather and climate.
'rays' is pinned to sunlight. The page glosses it as rayos straight after 'lightning', but
in English 'rays' means beams of sun almost exclusively — rayo as a lightning bolt is
'bolt'. Left alone this is the same trap as 'sleep'/lagaña on page 07.
Three section headers reduced to their head nouns: THE FOUR SEASONS -> seasons, THE
WEATHER -> weather, THE WEATHER FORECAST -> forecast.
autumn/fall (otoño, British against American) and snow/flurries (nieve) are collision
pairs. Unit 6 is almost entirely collisions — cold/cool/chill are all frío and
warmth/heat are both calor — which is exactly what makes it the most useful unit here.
'temperature' also appears in Health and Illness as body temperature. Different areas, and
VERY_EASY: an A1/A2 course, still its early pages.

area.name: The Weather
area.description: Hablar del tiempo: las estaciones, la lluvia y la nieve, el pronóstico, y todas las formas de decir que hace frío o calor.

units.name: The four seasons
units.topic: The four parts of the year and the word for the set of them. 'autumn' and 'fall' are the same season — one British, one American — and the unit should say so plainly

units.name: Weather, climate and degrees
units.topic: Talking about how hot or cold it is and how it is measured. 'weather' is what it is like today and 'climate' is what it is like all year — the same difference Spanish makes between tiempo and clima, and the unit should make it clear

units.name: Rain, snow and storms
units.topic: What falls from the sky and what a storm sounds and looks like. 'rays' here means the lines of light that come from the sun, NOT a lightning bolt — describe it that way. 'flurries' is light snow that does not settle

units.name: Sky, sun and wind
units.topic: What you see and feel outside on an ordinary day, and the things a warm day brings with it

units.name: The weather forecast
units.topic: The adjectives a forecast uses, each one built from the name of the thing itself by adding -y

units.name: Hot and cold
units.topic: Every way to say hot or cold. Spanish uses one word where English uses several: cold, cool and chill are all frío, and warmth and heat are both calor. The unit exists to separate them — cool is pleasantly cold, chill is a sudden cold you feel, chilly describes a person or a day that feels cold
